about: The first simulated pool (ops/deploy_sim.py check, then pool): six sizes, 5 000, 10 000, 25 000, 50 000, 100 000 and 250 000, each on the four tiers of the menu of 13 November 2026 (loss limit / target 3 / 9, 4 / 10, 5 / 10, 6 / 10 %), 24 lines, each with its own loss limit and target for both stages, the loss limit trailing the highest daily snapshot up to the starting balance (drawdown_kind 1). Prices from the CFO's menu (25 000 and up: the CFO's section on large accounts, 16 November 2026), payout 8 % of the size. 1 600 locked by the creator (locked_usdc), two payouts of the line of 10 000 (Alex, 11 November 2026): the lines of 5 000 and 10 000 on (on), the others off until the creator switches them on with two of their payouts free. Two payouts a day. Each line's tier replaces the stages' max_drawdown_bps and targets_bps below; the rest is both stages' own: daily loss 3 % from the day's snapshot, leverage by the rule v1.3. Thirty days a stage, and max_idle_s the same thirty days: the factory needs it set, and set to the stage's length it never ends a stage before its deadline, so the terms name no idle rule. A fill costs 450 ppm, Hyperliquid's taker fee, with no builder fee: nothing here trades on the exchange. Fills at the book, at most 150 bp worse than the oracle (the books stood 77 to 118 bp off it on 11 November 2026). fill_delay: 4 blocks, so that seeing the price a block ahead of the oracle gains a trader nothing (the CFO, 13 November 2026). fill_window: 3 blocks, a placeholder for a filler that is never late, until the keeper's --measure gives its largest lateness and the window is set from it (docs/SIM-POOL.md, Measuring the filler's window). codes: empty here on purpose; each trading group's code, the address its owner gave and its share go in before the pool sells (ops/deploy_sim.py codes), the shares from the CFO and Alex.
terms_text: Trading exams on Hyperliquid mainnet (HyperEVM). Both stages are trading exams on nobody's money: no real money is traded in them, an exam's price buys the exam and nothing else, and nothing here promises any gain. Each line of the menu is a size with its own loss limit and target, the same for both stages, and its price: 3 % and 9 %: 5 000 for 20 USDC, 10 000 for 40 USDC, 25 000 for 100 USDC, 50 000 for 200 USDC, 100 000 for 400 USDC, 250 000 for 1 000 USDC; 4 % and 10 %: 5 000 for 30 USDC, 10 000 for 60 USDC, 25 000 for 150 USDC, 50 000 for 300 USDC, 100 000 for 600 USDC, 250 000 for 1 500 USDC; 5 % and 10 %: 5 000 for 40 USDC, 10 000 for 79 USDC, 25 000 for 198 USDC, 50 000 for 395 USDC, 100 000 for 790 USDC, 250 000 for 1 975 USDC; 6 % and 10 %: 5 000 for 50 USDC, 10 000 for 95 USDC, 25 000 for 238 USDC, 50 000 for 475 USDC, 100 000 for 950 USDC, 250 000 for 2 375 USDC. The pool opens with the lines of 5 000 and 10 000 switched on; the lines of 25 000, 50 000, 100 000 and 250 000 are there and switched off. Only the pool's creator switches a line on, and only when the pool holds free money for two payouts of that line: 4 000 for 25 000, 8 000 for 50 000, 16 000 for 100 000, 40 000 for 250 000. Until the pool holds that money, the line cannot be switched on. Free money is what the pool holds less the payouts it owes, sets aside or keeps for stops, and the payouts of every trader who has passed an exam or runs a stage. A line that is on sells only while the pool holds free money for two of its payouts: while it does not, the line does not sell, and it sells again when the money is back. The creator may switch a line off at any time; an exam already bought keeps its rules. Each stage has a loss limit of the line's percent of its starting balance. It is measured from the highest equity recorded at the start of a UTC day (in the first 15 minutes of the UTC day), and it never rises above the starting balance: once the account's recorded equity is that percent above the start, the limit stays at the starting balance. Each stage also has: a target of the line's percent of the size; a daily loss of no more than 3 % below the day's first snapshot (equity including open positions, taken in the first 15 minutes of the UTC day); leverage at most 10x on BTC and ETH and 5x on SOL; thirty days at most, with no minimum of trading days. An order is filled by the platform's filler no sooner than the fourth block after the one it is placed in, at the price of the block that fills it, and lapses at no cost if it is not filled within 3 blocks from then. A fill takes the book's price, never better than the oracle's and at most 1.5 % worse, and pays 0.045 % of its notional, Hyperliquid's taker fee. Whoever passes the exam starts the stage within seven days; whoever passes the stage is paid a fixed 8 % of the size, once, which is not a share of any trading result: no sooner than 72 hours after the payout is claimed, and then once the pool's approver has approved it, or 7 days after it is claimed without approval. The platform's keeper claims a payout as soon as the stage has passed; a payout that may be paid is paid by a call anyone may make, which the keeper makes pass after pass. Each pool pays at most two payouts a day; any more are paid in order on the following days. The two are counted over any 24 hours and count every payout, approved or not: a payout whose 72 hours or 7 days have passed still waits for a following day once the day's two are paid. Payouts are paid in the order they were claimed, out of the money the pool holds: one still waiting for its approval keeps its place, and a later one is paid past it only if the money also covers every payout so passed over; one the pool cannot cover waits, and every payout after it, until money comes in. The pool's creator may change its approver at any time; whoever approves, no payout waits for approval longer than 7 days after it is claimed. Until it is paid, the platform's checker may stop it, once, with one of four reasons written on chain: 1, opposite positions with another account of the platform; 2, that, and the two wallets linked; 3, a result disputed: a flaw of the exam, the oracle or the filler; 4, prohibited play: a series of exams bought to trade each at the edge of its risk, or one account hedged by another, shown by transactions and a published analysis, with 14 days for the trader to object. A stopped payout stays in the pool for at least 14 days while the trader can object, unless the platform's operator lifts the stop within them and it is paid as any payout; after them anyone may make the stop final, and only from then is the money the pool's. Every exam is bought with a trading group's code, which the pool's creator sets with the address of the group's owner and the code's share, none or 40 to 60 %, and, for a code for two, an author's address and the author's part of that share; a pool has as many codes as its creator sets. Once a trader has used a code, its owner, its author and their split never change and its share can be raised, never lowered. When the creator takes money out of the pool, each code is credited its share of the surplus taken (what is above the payouts owed, held and kept, and above what the creator put in, less the platform's part) in the part of every price the pool took that its code's sales brought. What a code is credited stays in the pool, out of the creator's reach and out of payouts, until anyone sends it on, at any time: to the code's owner, and the author's part to the author. The platform takes 0.5 % of each price and of each withdrawal, and 1 HYPE to open the pool. The pool runs at least 6 months (184 days) from its opening: before then its creator can neither close it nor take back what it put in, only the surplus above it, and only the platform can close it sooner, with the money going where it would anyway. The creator withdraws by a request: the money leaves no sooner than 7 days after it, within 3 days after that, only what the pool can spare then, and never more than was asked; the platform may cancel a withdrawal request; it never moves the money. While the pool is open, the payout of a trader who has passed the exam stays in the pool from the pass, and for as long as the stage runs; the creator takes surplus only above every such payout, and above three payouts of the largest line that has an exam or a stage running, or is switched on and selling. A share credited to a code is never taken back, even if later payouts take the pool's money below what the creator put in. USDC sent to the pool other than by the creator's addToPot is not counted as put in by the creator: it covers payouts as any money of the pool does, and what of it is surplus when the creator takes money out (above the payouts owed, held and kept, and above what the creator put in) is shared with the codes' owners as any surplus taken.
